# Package `thaumcraft.api.client`

[All packages](README.md)

The client-only part of the Thaumcraft API: the particles that 1.7.10 add-ons drew through `Thaumcraft.proxy` (`thaumcraft.api.client.ThaumcraftClientFX`) and the tag of an aspect in a screen (`thaumcraft.api.client.AspectRenderer`).

Nothing here changes the world. `ThaumcraftClientFX` may be called from shared code (a server level is a no-op); `AspectRenderer` names client classes and belongs in client code only.

Types: [`AspectRenderer`](#aspectrenderer), [`ThaumcraftClientFX`](#thaumcraftclientfx)

## AspectRenderer

```java
public final class AspectRenderer
```

Draws the tag of an aspect in a screen or a HUD, the way Thaumcraft's own screens draw it.

This is the 1.21.1 counterpart of `thaumcraft.client.lib.UtilsFX.drawTag`, the helper every 1.7.10 add-on with a screen that listed aspects called (an analyser, a research table, a tooltip). **Client only:** the class names `GuiGraphics`, which a dedicated server does not have, so load it only from client code (a screen, a HUD callback, a Fabric `client` entrypoint, a NeoForge `Dist.CLIENT` class). The geometry constants below are plain compile-time constants and can be read from anywhere.

**Geometry.** The tag is a square of `TAG_SIZE` (16) pixels whose top left corner is the `x`, `y` you pass, in the coordinate space of the `GuiGraphics` (scaled GUI pixels, the pose stack applies):
- the glyph `aspect.getImage()` is stretched over `(x, y)` to `(x + 16, y + 16)` and tinted with `aspect.getColor()`. An `Aspect` cannot be built without a texture location, so there is always a glyph to draw; if the file behind the location is missing, the square shows the game's missing-texture checkerboard, as any texture that fails to load does;
- **amount**: above zero, the number is drawn at half size, white with a shadow, so that its right edge is the right edge of the glyph (`x +` `AMOUNT_RIGHT`) and its top is `AMOUNT_TOP` (11) pixels below `y`; it sits in front of the glyph and in front of an item drawn at the same place (depth +200). Zero or less draws no number. This is the number of the research book and the table: *no* `+`, no thousands separator;
- **bonus**: above zero, the sparkle of the research table is drawn over the top left corner of the glyph, a 16 by 16 frame whose top left corner is `BONUS_OFFSET` (-4) pixels from the tag's on both axes; it cycles through sixteen frames of the particle sheet, one per tick of the local player. Above one, the bonus is also written as a half size number centred on `x +` `BONUS_NUMBER_CENTER_X` (4) with its top `BONUS_NUMBER_TOP` (3) pixels below `y`, in front of the sparkle.

The tag is not clipped, not scaled to the screen and gives no tooltip: the add-on decides where it is, whether the mouse is over it (a `TAG_SIZE` square) and what the hover shows. To draw it larger or smaller, scale the pose stack around `x`, `y` first.

Blending is enabled while the tag is drawn and left enabled (the book relies on it); the colour of the graphics is reset to white. Call it from the render thread only, between the begin and the end of a frame of the GUI.

**Differences from the original.** `draw` is `UtilsFX.drawTag` with the blend, the alpha and the black and white switch left out, and **the amount is an `int`**: the original took a `float` and showed up to two decimals (`DecimalFormat("#######.##")` in the audited legacy source of this repository), so a fraction of an essentia showed there and does not here. The top of the amount is the whole pixel `AMOUNT_TOP` (11), where that source starts its line of text at `y + 11.5`.

**Verification.** The numbers above are asserted by unit tests (the order of the arguments, the thresholds of the amount and of the bonus and the text of the numbers go through a pure layout object that the renderer reads); the pixels have *not yet been inspected on a rendered frame* (see section 9 of `docs/audit/KNOWN_DEVIATIONS.md`): the tag and its amount are the code the research book already uses for its aspect rows, and the bonus sparkle follows the one the research table draws on its palette.

<a id="aspectrenderer-draw"></a>
```java
public static void draw(GuiGraphics graphics, Aspect aspect, int x, int y, int amount, int bonus)
```

Original `UtilsFX.drawTag(x, y, aspect, amount, bonus, zLevel, blend, alpha, bw)` with the blend, the alpha and the black and white switch left out, and with an `int` amount (the original took a `float`): draws the tag of an aspect with its amount and its bonus at a position of a GUI.

**Throws:** `NullPointerException` — when `aspect` is not `null` and `graphics` is `null`

**Parameters:**
- `graphics` — the graphics of the frame being drawn (the `GuiGraphics` a screen's `render` or a HUD callback is given); must not be `null` when an aspect is drawn
- `aspect` — the aspect; `null` draws nothing
- `x` — the left edge of the tag, in GUI pixels
- `y` — the top edge of the tag, in GUI pixels
- `amount` — the whole number shown at the bottom right corner; zero or less shows none
- `bonus` — zero or less shows no bonus, one shows the sparkle, more shows the sparkle and the number

## ThaumcraftClientFX

```java
public final class ThaumcraftClientFX
```

The client-side particle effects of Thaumcraft that 1.7.10 add-ons drew through `Thaumcraft.proxy`: the sparkle, the burst, the wisp, the block runes, the continuous beam, the smoke spiral and the essentia trail.

**Client only.** These draw on the client; the 1.7.10 `CommonProxy` had empty bodies for them, and so does this class on a server: a call with a server level (or with `null`) draws nothing and does not fail. Only the signatures name common types, so this class loads on a dedicated server without any client class (the client classes are reached only from a call with a client level). Call it from the **client thread** (a block's `animateTick`, an item's `inventoryTick` or `use` on the client, a client tick or render callback); on a client level from any other thread it throws `IllegalStateException`, because the particle engine is not thread safe. To make every nearby client draw an effect that the server decides on, call the server twins in `thaumcraft.api.ThaumcraftFX` (`sparkle`, `burst`, `blockRunes`, `smokeSpiral`, `essentiaTrail`).

**Units.** Positions are world coordinates in blocks (doubles) unless a method says "block"; sizes are the particle scale of the original (`1` is the ordinary size, the originals used 0.1 to 3); durations and lifetimes are game ticks; colours are `0xRRGGBB` ints (the bits above the low 24 are ignored) or float components from 0 to 1 (a finite component outside that range is clamped to it); gravity is the original unit, the particle falls by `0.04 * gravity` per tick (negative rises).

**Arguments.** Every method checks its arguments first, on every side, and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a non-finite number (a colour component included), a coordinate outside the world, a size of zero or less, a type outside its range or a duration that is not positive, so a mistake shows in a server-only test too and cannot put NaN into the particle engine. The ranges are the constants of `thaumcraft.common.lib.fx.ClientFxRules` and are repeated in each method.

**Particle setting.** The sparkle and the beam honour the player's particle setting as the originals did (nothing at "minimal"); `particleCount` is the original `particleCount(base)` for add-on code that loops. The other effects draw whatever the add-on asks for, as the originals did: the caller thins them with `particleCount`.

**Not here.** The original proxy also had `wispFX4` (a wisp that homes on an entity), `beamPulseFX`, `bolt`, `arcLightning`, `crucibleBubble`, `blockWard`, `infusedStoneSparkle` and the infusion particles; they are internal to Thaumcraft's own effects and have no facade. The beam returns no handle (see `beam`).

**Verification.** The argument rules and the geometry of the pure parts are asserted by unit tests; the particles themselves have *not yet been inspected on a rendered frame* (see section 9 of `docs/audit/KNOWN_DEVIATIONS.md`): they are the very particle classes Thaumcraft's own effects use, but a facade call that works is not a screenshot of how it looks.

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-particlecount"></a>
```java
public static int particleCount(Level level, int base)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.particleCount(base)`: how many particles a loop of the add-on should draw at the player's particle setting. `0` at "minimal", `base` at "decreased", `2 * base` at "all". Always `0` for a server level or `null`.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — when `base` is negative

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a level; only a client level gives a non-zero answer
- `base` — the count the add-on wants at the decreased setting, zero or more

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-sparkle"></a>
```java
public static void sparkle(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float size, int type, float gravity)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.sparkle(x, y, z, size, color, gravity)`: one sparkle, the glittering quad that shrinks away over 18 ticks (`3 * 6`) and falls by `0.04 * gravity` per tick. The sparkle is drawn only on a roll: with the particle setting at "all" four rolls of six draw it, at "decreased" two of six, at "minimal" none, so a caller that wants a sure sparkle calls it several times, as the originals did.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `x` — the position, in blocks
- `y` — the position, in blocks
- `z` — the position, in blocks
- `size` — the scale, above 0 and at most 16 (the originals used 0.5 to 2)
- `type` — the colour, 0 to 7 (the `color` index of the original): 0 violet, 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green, 4 red, 5 black (drawn like smoke), 6 white, 7 cyan; each with the small random variation of the original
- `gravity` — how fast it falls; 0 hangs in the air, a negative number rises

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-sparkle-2"></a>
```java
public static void sparkle(Level level, double x, double y, double z, int type)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.sparkle(x, y, z, color)`: `sparkle(Level, double, double, double, float, int, float)` with the size `1.5` and no gravity. (The size is the one of the audited legacy source of this repository; the 1.7.10 jar was not available to confirm it.)

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `type` — the colour, 0 to 7, see the long form

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-burst"></a>
```java
public static void burst(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float size)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.burst(world, x, y, z, scale)`: the white puff of the wisp and the shock orb, a flipbook of 32 frames that plays for 31 ticks at three quarters opacity. It is drawn in vanilla's particle layer, not in Thaumcraft's, so the particle setting does not thin it.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `size` — the scale of the puff, which is its half size, above 0 and at most 16 (the originals used 0.5 to 3)

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-wisp"></a>
```java
public static void wisp(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float size, float red, float green, float blue)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.wispFX(world, x, y, z, size, red, green, blue)`: one mote of the wisp in any colour. It lives about 36 to 51 ticks, grows to full size by half its life and shrinks again, drifts with gravity `0.02`, is pushed out of solid blocks and is not drawn farther from the camera than 50 blocks (25 on fast graphics). A red of exactly 0 is drawn as 1, a quirk of the original.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `size` — the scale, above 0 and at most 16 (the wisp entity uses 0.1)
- `red` — 0 to 1; any finite value is accepted and one outside that range is clamped to it
- `green` — 0 to 1, clamped like `red`
- `blue` — 0 to 1, clamped like `red`

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-wisp-2"></a>
```java
public static void wisp(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float size, int type, boolean shrink, boolean noClip, float gravity)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.wispFX2(world, x, y, z, size, type, shrink, clip, gravity)`: one mote of a primal colour that drifts with the given gravity.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `size` — the scale, above 0 and at most 16
- `type` — the colour, 0 to 5: the six colours of the original wisps, 5 being the dark one that is drawn like smoke
- `shrink` — `true` fades the mote out over its whole life; `false` grows it to full size at half its life and shrinks it again
- `noClip` — `true` lets it pass through blocks (the original `clip` argument set `noClip`)
- `gravity` — how fast it falls; negative rises

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-wisp-3"></a>
```java
public static void wisp(Level level, double x, double y, double z, double tx, double ty, double tz, float size, int type, boolean shrink, float gravity)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.wispFX3(world, x, y, z, tx, ty, tz, size, type, shrink, speed)`: one mote of a primal colour that sets off from the first point towards the second at the speed that would cover the distance in its lifetime (36 to 51 ticks). Like every wisp it loses 2% of its speed each tick, so it ends short of the second point, and it falls with the gravity it is given. The parameter the original called the count is the colour `type`, and `speed` is the gravity.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `tx` — the point it flies to, in blocks
- `ty` — the point it flies to, in blocks
- `tz` — the point it flies to, in blocks
- `size` — the scale, above 0 and at most 16
- `type` — the colour, 0 to 5, see the shorter form
- `shrink` — see the shorter form
- `gravity` — how fast it falls on its way; negative rises

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-blockrunes"></a>
```java
public static void blockRunes(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float red, float green, float blue, int duration, float gravity)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.blockRunes(world, x, y, z, red, green, blue, duration, gravity)`: one rune glyph that fades in and out, as the warding stone and the thaumometer scan draw it.

**The position is the corner of a block, not a point.** The original added half a block on every axis, so the rune is placed relative to `(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, z + 0.5)`: pass the block's own coordinates and add the height you want above the block to `y`: to put the rune just above the top face of the block at `(bx, by, bz)` pass `(bx, by + 0.7, bz)`, which is `1.2` above the bottom of the block. The glyph is a flat quad drawn upright against a randomly chosen side of the block whose middle is that point, one of sixteen glyphs, with a small random offset in its own plane, as the original did. It is not thinned by the particle setting: loop over `particleCount` as the original callers did.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `red` — 0 to 1; any finite value is accepted and one outside that range is clamped to it
- `green` — 0 to 1, clamped like `red`
- `blue` — 0 to 1, clamped like `red`
- `duration` — 1 to 6000; the rune lives three times this many ticks, fading in over the first fifth
- `gravity` — the rune's vertical speed changes by `-0.04 * gravity` every tick: a negative gravity lifts it, as the `-0.02` of Thaumcraft's own runes does

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-beam"></a>
```java
public static void beam(Level level, Entity owner, Vec3 from, Vec3 to, int rgb, int type, boolean reverse, float endScale, int impact)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.beamCont(world, player, tx, ty, tz, type, color, reverse, endmod, input, impact)`: a continuous beam of light, the one the focus of excavation draws, from one point to another. It is three crossed ribbons that turn about the beam's axis, the texture sliding along them, ending in a glint when `impact` is above zero.

**Call it every client tick while the beam should show.** A beam lasts 8 ticks from its first call, and each further call for the same `owner` moves it to the new ends and makes it last at least 4 more ticks, which is what the original did with the beam object it returned (and took back as `input`); there is no handle to keep, and a beam is simply let go by not calling. One owner has one beam at a time: a second call for the same entity moves that beam and changes its colour, so two beams from one player need two owners. The beam ends at once when `owner` is removed or the start of the beam is more than 64 blocks from the local player, and is dropped when the level changes. At most 32 beams are kept; the oldest goes first. It honours the particle setting: at "minimal" nothing is drawn.

**The impact counts down, and the call phase matters.** Thaumcraft steps every beam once at the end of each client tick (the `CLIENT_POST` listener of Architectury, in the order of registration), and the step lowers `impact` by one, as the update of the original particle did. A call that runs *before* that step in the same tick, as the callers of the original did (an item's or entity's client tick, a block's tick, a network task, the start of the client tick), is drawn with the value you passed minus one, so a 1 is gone before it is drawn. A call that runs *after* it (a listener of the end of the client tick registered after Thaumcraft's, or a render callback) is drawn with the full value: the glint is a step larger and fainter than the original's. Pick one phase and keep to it; the example add-on calls it from the start of the client tick.

The original drew the beam from the tip of the wand in the player's hand, which it worked out itself. This form takes the start from the caller; the form that takes a `Player` works it out the way the original did, see `wandTip`.

**Throws:** `NullPointerException` — when `owner`, `from` or `to` is `null`

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges above (a texture outside 0 to 3, an `endScale` outside 0 to 8, an `impact` outside 0 to 5, a non-finite end), also when `level` is not a client level; checked before `owner` is looked at

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `owner` — the entity the beam belongs to (the player whose focus it is), in `level`
- `from` — where the beam starts, in blocks
- `to` — where it ends, in blocks
- `rgb` — the colour, `0xRRGGBB`
- `type` — the texture, 0 to 3 (`beam`, `beam1`, `beam2`, `beam3`); the excavation focus uses 2
- `reverse` — whether the texture slides from the end to the start
- `endScale` — the width of the far end relative to the start, 0 to 8 (0 narrows the beam to a point), and, with `impact`, the size of the glint; the excavation focus uses 2 on a hit and 0 otherwise
- `impact` — 0 draws no glint at the far end; above 0 draws one of the size `endScale / 2 / (6 - impact)`, which grows with the value. The value counts down by one every client tick (see above), so pass 5 on every call while the beam hits something, as Thaumcraft's own foci do, and 0 while it does not

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-beam-2"></a>
```java
public static void beam(Level level, Player owner, Vec3 to, int rgb, int type, boolean reverse, float endScale, int impact)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.beamCont(world, player, tx, ty, tz, type, color, reverse, endmod, input, impact)` as it was called: a beam from the tip of the wand of `owner` (`wandTip`) to a point. Everything else is as in `beam(Level, Entity, Vec3, Vec3, int, int, boolean, float, int)`: call it every client tick, there is no handle, and one player has one beam.

**Throws:** `NullPointerException` — when `owner` or `to` is `null`

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for the ranges of the long form

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `owner` — the player whose wand it is, in `level`
- `to` — where the beam ends, in blocks

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-wandtip"></a>
```java
public static Vec3 wandTip(Player player)
```

Where the beam of a wand starts: the tip of the wand in the hand of a player, as the original `FXBeamWand` worked it out and as the excavation focus of Thaumcraft sends it to the clients: the eye, moved `0.066` against the cosine and `0.04` against the sine of the yaw (in radians), `0.06` down, and `0.3` along the look vector. It does not look at the hand the wand is in or at the camera (the first-person model and the third-person one differ); it is the same point for every viewer. Pure arithmetic: it works on any side.

**Throws:** `NullPointerException` — when `player` is `null`

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-smokespiral"></a>
```java
public static void smokeSpiral(Level level, double x, double y, double z, float radius, int start, int minY, int rgb)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.smokeSpiral(world, x, y, z, radius, start, miny, color)`: **one** puff of smoke that travels along a spiral, turning twice about the point while it sinks from the top to the bottom of a sphere of that radius, and fades out. It lives 20 to 29 ticks. One call draws one puff, not a ring: the Sword of the Zephyr calls it 5 times and the awakening eldritch warden 33 times, each time with a random `start` angle, and the puffs together make the ring. Loop, and give each call its own `start`.

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `x` — the centre of the sphere, in blocks
- `y` — the centre of the sphere, in blocks
- `z` — the centre of the sphere, in blocks
- `radius` — the radius in blocks, 0 to 64
- `start` — the angle in degrees at which the turn starts (the originals pass a random 0 to 359)
- `minY` — the lowest y, in blocks, the smoke may sink to (a floor): it never draws below `minY + 0.1`
- `rgb` — the colour, `0xRRGGBB`

<a id="thaumcraftclientfx-essentiatrail"></a>
```java
public static void essentiaTrail(Level level, BlockPos from, BlockPos to, int phase, int rgb, float scale)
```

The original `Thaumcraft.proxy.essentiaTrailFx(world, x, y, z, tx, ty, tz, count, color, scale)`: one glowing mote of essentia that leaves the middle of one block, wobbles on its way to the middle of another and dies when it arrives. The original was called once or twice a tick to make a stream; a single call makes a single mote. (To show a running transfer between two blocks, ask the server with `thaumcraft.api.ThaumcraftFX.essentiaTrail`.)

**Throws:** `NullPointerException` — when `from` or `to` is `null`

**Parameters:**
- `level` — a client level; anything else draws nothing
- `from` — the block the mote starts in
- `to` — the block it flies to; farther than 64 blocks from `from` nothing is drawn
- `phase` — the original `count`: the wobble of the mote follows `sin(phase / 2)`, `sin(phase / 3)` and `sin(phase / 4)`, so pass a running counter (the age of the block entity) to make a stream curl
- `rgb` — the colour, `0xRRGGBB`, usually `aspect.getColor()`
- `scale` — the size, above 0 and at most 16 (the originals used 0.5 to 1)
